Gate tokens are now content-addressable (cache.rkt token-address): a 'token input hashes to the digest of its producer gate's recorded cache entry — the recipe identity + input hashes + code hashes of the gate's last PASSING run. An unchanged upstream (and unchanged gate rule/code/runtime) yields an unchanged token, so dbt-build can finally cache-skip; anything that moves the gate moves the token, surfaced on the consumer AS the token ('input-changed (tok)). Conservative by construction: no producer / no entry / an entry without a snapshot (the gate's own inputs weren't addressable) -> #f -> the consumer stays 'inputs-unresolvable, so an unaddressed verdict propagates and never launders into a false skip. Setup: the offline suffix place-marts -> species-export -> species-maps, run against
the local dbt sandbox marts with --export-dir pointed at a scratch dir (never a
served one). species-maps is a real 785-key 'dir fan-out (591 species + 194 group
maps, 32 MB of SVG). Five builds recorded, builds 19-23.

What it proved:

1. THE ROLL-UP IS THE PARTS' ADDRESS, on real data. The recorded output digest for
   species-maps and its keyed-map block CID are the SAME string
   (bafyreih3w7wwbkoprtj4ojh7v6pmqssecxhqj5bcb4xcogy5ytapfqtsmy) — the "one object"
   property, not merely two values that agree.

2. DEDUP. Re-producing an identical map added NO block (3 -> 3). Restoring a reverted
   input also added none (4 -> 4): the earlier block was reused, so a revert is free.
   Five observations of a 785-key map cost 4 blocks / 120 KB, and the log line grew
   9 KB total across five build records — inline it would have carried ~52 KB per
   observation.

3. --moved-keys, THE POINT OF THE WHOLE THING. Dropping one species' occurrences
   (bombus mixtus) named exactly 5 of 785 keys: Bombus/mixtus.svg plus its four
   ancestor group maps — genus/Bombus, subgenus/Bombus/Pyrobombus, tribe/Bombini,
   subfamily/Apinae. Taxonomically correct, not merely non-empty. Machine-readable
   keys on stdout, prose on stderr, exit 0.

4. THE REFUSALS. A first production answered 'no-basis and exit 1 ("every key is new,
   which is not a delta. Rebuild in full") rather than exit 0 with silence.

5. --block dumped the real 785-key map, and --history species-maps rendered the full
   per-key timeline off the blocks.

THE MOVE PAID FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY by falsifying st-zb9's premise. cache-test.rkt:163 builds a task that PRODUCES an 'authoritative artifact — which is not a test artifact but the exact case cache.rkt's provenance filter exists for ('Authoritative outputs are excluded — cutoff applies only to derived state'). It only looked correct because beeatlas has none today. leaf-expectation is now three-valued ('leaf / 'produced / 'either) and ADR 0013 D2 records the error.

The main.rkt asymmetry is resolved as principled, not historical: check-partial-tasks needs the partial-task list and check-dir-extents needs a path resolver, so neither is pure over the graph alone and neither can move without dragging that context in. Recorded in ADR 0013's consequences.

Declined, deliberately — the question is now decided rather than dropped a second time, which was the point of filing it.

The asymmetry is principled. A dangling REFERENCE (a task edge naming an artifact nobody declared) changes behaviour silently: the edge vanishes from the plan and the task stops being invalidated by that input. That is now impossible (st-5e6). A dangling DECLARATION (an artifact referenced by nothing) changes no behaviour at all — it is inert, and inert is visible on inspection rather than silent in a build.

The 'other half of a typo' case from the description turns out to be already covered: declare taxa.csv.gz, wire the task to taxa.csv, and st-5e6 fires on the task side of that pair. There is no pair where only the artifact side is wrong AND something breaks.

Against that, the cost is real: an unreferenced artifact is a legitimate transient state while authoring, and build-graph now runs on every module load, so it would fire mid-edit. Reopen if a concrete case appears where an unreferenced artifact caused a wrong result — none is known.

FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THIS ISSUE'S OWN PREMISE. It claimed verify-edges is 'called from nowhere outside its own module (grepped src/, 2026-08-06)'. That grep excluded src/edge-verify*, which hid src/edge-verify-integration-test.rkt — the harness DID have a caller, in the test suite, gated on a local reference build. So the gap was narrower than filed: not 'never runs' but 'runs only for a human who just built, over a hardcoded 7 tasks'. The lesson is the one this repo keeps relearning: an exclusion pattern that hides the thing you are asking about produces a confident wrong answer.

WHAT LANDED:
- --verify-edges in main.rkt. No target; runs the covered set against the scratch dir or --export-dir.
- The task list moved from the test into beeatlas.rkt (beeatlas-edge-verify-tasks). Two copies would let the unattended run and the test disagree about coverage, and the one covering less would look identical.
- verify-edges no longer aborts the run when one task's seeds are missing. verify-edge is RIGHT to raise (an incomplete reference is a harness precondition, not an edge defect), but the driver was letting one missing file abandon every task after it — which for an unattended run reports on a prefix and reads like a clean run of that prefix. Now reported as UNVERIFIABLE, counted separately, denominator is tasks ASKED not tasks that ran.
- Exit non-zero on a bad edge OR an incomplete reference. Deliberately not advisory: an exit code that is always 0 is a check nobody notices. A caller that wants it advisory says '|| true' itself — policy at the caller, signal in the tool.
- Reports what it does NOT cover. Measured: 7 covered of 13 candidate tasks (a candidate = subprocess recipe + at least one EXPORT_DIR output).

VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT, not by reading it: 3/7 clean, 4 unverifiable against a partial local reference, 6 uncovered named, exit 1.

NOT DONE, deliberately: adding the nightly call. That is a one-line change in beeatlas's nightly.sh and beeatlas is a test bed, not ours to edit as a side effect. The CLI is the part that had to exist first.

Closed by the runtime-identity probe: a runtime may declare a probe argv (node --version) run THROUGH its own launch prefix; the resolved interpreter's trimmed output rides each task's input address on the code side as 'runtime:<name>' (raw version string, ABSENT-ADDRESS argument), so a patch bump inside .nvmrc's range or a no-nvm PATH fallback reads as code-changed naming it. Decision made: this is an INPUT OBSERVATION at snapshot time through an injected build-env resolver (like resolve-relation's DuckDB digest) — planning observes, never executes; an exec-time probe could never close a wrong-skip because exec never runs on a skip. Observation only, never a version gate (nvm already enforces the pin at exec where present; Stelis parsing range semantics would be a hand-kept mirror). Probe failure or no resolver = inputs-unresolvable forced run, keeping planning total. Memoized once per env. node only: uv run can sync the venv and dbt's uvx can hit the network at plan time, so each needs its own decision (e.g. a --no-sync variant) before getting a probe — recorded in the runtime's comment. .nvmrc stays hashed (intent vs. reality).
